bearings.system_side: The L-LV family regresses sector LobbyView lobbying in real 2025 USD millions (dv lobby_lv_real_m, the de-duplicated primary column) on lagged sector growth. The log forms (R-log) are separate robustness fits, so the base model is in levels, not logs. The R-yearFE variant swaps national controls for sector and year fixed effects. The recorded result that the lobbying lead flips sign under year FE was not found in the sector_growth_study markdown files checked here.

bearings.transfer_conditions: Design warning only. If lobbying feeds revenue, a growth-to-lobbying regression is simultaneous, so OLS with fixed effects cannot sign the lead. The paper's IV is 4.5 to 7.3 times its OLS (0.227/0.0500 = 4.5; 0.319/0.0436 = 7.3), not 4.5 to 7. The paper uses Compustat public firms with federal LDA filings 1999-2015 and no trade associations, while the sector panel includes associations, so the effect size does not transfer. The paper does not say how it handles self-filer and outside-firm double counting; the text mentions only that about 85 percent of lobbying is outsourced.
bearings.verifier_note: Coefficients, F-stats, SEs, N and the preferred-column statement reproduce from Table 2. Corrections: base sector model is in levels not logs; IV/OLS ratio range is 4.5 to 7.3. The sign-flip result was not reproduced.

bearings.paper_claim: LDA client names were matched to Compustat in four steps: FuzzyWuzzy against 61,478 unique client names; Bureau van Dijk batch search for ISIN and ticker; CRP standardized client names; and a random 5 percent sample of client names checked for publicly traded firms that were missed. The 5 percent sample is a miss (recall) check, not a precision audit. The paper names messy spellings and abbreviations as the main hazard. The matched universe is 67,842 unique lobbying client names (Introduction).

bearings.system_side: classify_client assigns Bank, CU or other. Credit-union names are checked first and are decisive, then trade-association names, then bank names with exclusions. Only when no name rule fires does the function fall back to a NAICS-based side. So NAICS does drive side assignment as a fallback, not only linkage metadata. No random-sample accuracy audit of the classification is recorded.

related.why: LobbyView is the firm-name-disambiguated LDA and bill database that this paper builds on and releases (confirmed from the item title). Ingestion by collect_lobbyview.py was not checked.
Same LobbyView firm linkage, joined to FEC donations, bearing on the lobbying-to-contribution relation in H&K Fact 2. Checked only by title and authors.
Uses bill-level LobbyView data of the kind H&K use for committee shares and clients per bill (median 2). Checked only by title and authors.
Survey of empirical lobbying models, including returns-to-lobbying designs and the Grossman-Helpman microfoundation that H&K Section 3.2 generalizes.
Links corporate lobbying and PACs to market concentration, a related misallocation question at industry level. The outcome differs from H&K's firm-size distortion.
A single-policy lobbying ROI estimate. H&K's economy-wide revenue elasticity is a different target, so compare with care.
Its two-way fixed-effects caution applies to H&K's OLS columns (firm, year and state-year FE) and to the system's sector-growth regressions.
Finds low overlap between organizational lobbying and PAC spending, which qualifies any use of H&K's lobbying-to-contribution ratio.
Models committee assignment as a matching process, bearing on H&K's identifying assumption that committee moves are exogenous to firms.
Network analysis of House committees, relevant to H&K's committee-share weights. Checked only by title and authors.

summary_issues: Summary and gaps say the 5 percent random sample verifies classifier precision. The paper uses it to find publicly traded firms that were missed (recall), so the template is a recall audit.
Summary says NAICS is linkage metadata only and that the rules fail closed. classify_client falls back to a NAICS-based side when no name rule fires (collect_lobbyview.py lines 258-262).
Flags say the authors concede committee exogeneity may fail at p.26. The concession is on printed p.25 (annotation page 26).
Transfer text says the IV is 4.5 to 7 times OLS. The exact ratios are 4.5 (0.227/0.0500) and 7.3 (0.319/0.0436).
Summary says the 3 percent headline uses the full-sample estimate. That is arithmetically consistent (0.319 x 10) but the paper does not name the column, so present it as inference.
Summary describes the sector-growth base model as log sector lobbying. The base dv is lobby_lv_real_m in real 2025 USD millions; log forms are R-log robustness variants.
Summary says the 2007-2009 break is not in the backtest. It is outside the 2014-2023 targets but may be in training data; the backtest start year was not checked.
Summary says the lobbying lead flips sign under year fixed effects. No matching text was found in the sector_growth_study markdown files checked; not verified here.

Summary says Paul's positions cite H&K under the flip model, joint optimizer, workbook allocator, break-even, ROI, cycle model and employer match, and that several positions are stale. The item's Paul record (68 highlights, zero notes, zero takeaways) does not show this; not verified.
